clue.text: One after another, parents will find London street

indicators.note: the two parents are set one after another, each followed by the contracted will

parts.note: father will, contracted to Pa'll
mother will, contracted to Ma'll

explanation.surface: Mum and Dad, walking in turn, will come upon a famous London street.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'parents will' does double duty: each parent in turn, with the contracted will, set 'One after another'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pall Mall is a well-known street in the St James's area of central London, home of gentlemen's clubs.

clue.text: Neighbour employing a nanny, possibly

parts.note: a nanny goat is something that butts, so it may be called a butter

explanation.surface: Someone living next door has hired a childminder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nanny' suggests a childminder, but it is the goat, which butts with its horns.
explanation.definitionFit: One whose property abuts yours, borders it directly, is a neighbour.

clue.text: Girl takes up instrument that's found inside subaltern's office

indicators.note: in a down clue the girl sits beneath the rest, holding it up
the abbreviation for that's is placed within the instrument

parts.note: a lute is a stringed instrument
i.e. is short for id est, 'that is'
Nancy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl lifts a musical instrument discovered in a junior officer's quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is the Latin abbreviation id est; 'takes up' works because in a down clue the girl sits beneath, supporting the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenancy is the rank or post of a lieutenant, and a subaltern is a junior officer below captain.

clue.text: Cartographer's book, abridged after much delay

indicators.note: shortened, so the final letter of the phrase is cut off

parts.note: after a long wait is 'at last'

explanation.surface: A mapmaker's volume, finally published in a shortened form after long waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abridged' looks like it describes the book, but it trims the T from AT LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps, the essential volume of a cartographer.

clue.text: Ears give trouble? One catches the wind

parts.note: lugs is informal British slang for ears
to ail is to afflict or trouble

explanation.surface: Earache asks whether something is troubling someone's ears.
explanation.walkthrough: LUGS is British slang for ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A lugsail is a four-cornered sail hung from a yard, which catches the wind to drive a boat.

clue.text: Painful parting from girl touring Central America

indicators.note: going round, so the girl's letters surround the inner piece

parts.note: wench is an old word for a girl or young woman

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word America is taken

explanation.surface: A tearful farewell from a young woman travelling around Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central America' looks like the region, but it means the middle letter R of AMERICA.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is a sudden painful separation, emotionally hard to bear.

clue.text: Reserved, as one's underperforming savings may be?

definitions.meaning: shy and keeping to oneself, aloof

definitions.text: as one's underperforming savings may be?
definitions.meaning: money doing badly in an account may be taken out of it

explanation.definitionFit: Withdrawn means introverted and unforthcoming, and money removed from an account has been withdrawn.

clue.text: Prolonged period in English cricket side

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A long spell spent in an English cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immensely long stretch of time, an age.

clue.text: Body of man buried in estate

indicators.note: the man is put deep within the car

parts.note: an estate is a type of car, an estate car or station wagon
Dave is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man's corpse is found buried on a country estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'estate' suggests land, but it is the British name for a station wagon, a CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadaver is a dead body, a corpse, especially one used for dissection.

clue.text: Ignorant European needling hunt badly

indicators.note: done badly, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: An uninformed European is mocking a hunt that went poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' shuffles E with the letters of NEEDLING HUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unenlightened lacks knowledge or understanding, so is ignorant.

clue.text: Condition of some works of art out East

indicators.note: the letter for East is taken out of the works of art

parts.note: statues are works of art
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: The state of some artworks displayed out in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out East' reads as a location but removes E from STATUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's state or standing, a condition or position.

clue.text: Clubs abandoning habit-forming supplement

indicators.note: the clubs letter leaves the word

parts.note: something habit-forming is addictive
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A dietary supplement without which clubs would be more addictive.
explanation.walkthrough: C (clubs, the card suit) is dropped from ADDICTIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An additive is something added, a supplement to food or fuel.

clue.text: Newspaper hastening holiday home arrangement

parts.note: The Times is a British newspaper
haring means running fast like a hare

explanation.surface: A newspaper hurries to report on a deal over holiday homes.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's own paper gives TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Timesharing is joint ownership of a holiday property, each owner using it for a set period.

clue.text: Where some Spaniards live, consuming seedy fruit

indicators.note: eating, so the city swallows the other piece

parts.note: Granada is a city in southern Spain
seedy can mean unwell, ill

explanation.surface: In a Spanish town residents are eating a fruit full of seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seedy' seems to describe the fruit but means ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A granadilla is a passion fruit, the edible fruit of a passionflower.

clue.text: Put brake on horse-drawn carriage — it wings along

parts.note: to drag is to act as a brake, slowing something
a fly is a light one-horse carriage for hire

explanation.surface: Instructions to slow a horse-drawn coach.
explanation.walkthrough: A FLY was a one-horse hired carriage, an old British term.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect is a strong flier, darting along on its wings.

clue.text: An evangelist's goal

definitions.meaning: one of the four Gospel writers

explanation.definitionFit: Mark is the second Gospel writer, and a mark is a target one aims at.

clue.text: Scottish port Cockneys verbally confuse with London district?

indicators.note: a Cockney drops the H and slurs the vowels, so the district's name comes out sounding like the port

parts.note: Holborn is a district of central London

explanation.surface: East Enders mix up a Scottish harbour town with a London area.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are Londoners from the East End, known for dropping H: HOLBORN becomes 'OB'N.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a ferry port on the west coast of Scotland, gateway to the Hebrides.

clue.text: Sob loudly, being fat

definitions.meaning: the fat of whales and seals

explanation.definitionFit: To blubber is to cry noisily, and blubber is also the thick fat layer of marine mammals.

clue.text: Inside tram, it's wrong to run

indicators.note: put wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Within a tram it is improper to run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' looks like a container signal, but its letters join TRAM as anagram fodder for 'wrong'.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer an organisation is to manage or run it.

clue.text: Springtime examination of council leader

parts.note: May is a spring month
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A spring exam for the leader of the council.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayoral means relating to a mayor, the head of a town council.

clue.text: No longer erupting, divorcee can appear before court

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A divorced person can show up in court once the volcano is quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is the noun TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct volcano is one that will no longer erupt.

clue.text: Meddler unknown in transport organisation

indicators.note: the unknown is set within the transport organisation

parts.note: a bus is a means of transport
a body is an organised group
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An interfering person nobody knows works at the transport authority.
explanation.definitionFit: A busybody pries into others' affairs, a meddler.

clue.text: Virginal class admitting harpsichordists at first

indicators.note: letting in, so the class contains the other letter

parts.note: a caste is a social class

indicators.note: only the opening letter of harpsichordists is used

explanation.surface: A virginal class lets in harpsichord players first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virginal' looks like the keyboard instrument, fitting the harpsichordists, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure, sexually innocent, like a virgin.

clue.text: Freewheel along shore

definitions.meaning: to move without power, like a cyclist not pedalling

explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to move without effort or power, and the coast is the seashore.

clue.text: Support arrangement, but laze, possibly

parts.note: to back is to support
a formation is an arrangement

explanation.surface: A support structure was arranged, but people just lazed about.
explanation.walkthrough: A back-formation is a word made by stripping an apparent ending from an older word: laze from lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb laze was formed from lazy, an example of a word derived by removing a supposed suffix.

clue.text: Criminal has change of heart, seeing prison

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is replaced by another

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal

explanation.surface: A felon repents, realising jail awaits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of heart' sounds like repentance but swaps the middle letter of CON.
explanation.definitionFit: The can is American slang for prison or jail.

clue.text: Opening woman found in 17

indicators.note: the woman is placed inside the other word

parts.note: the answer at 17 means to sob, which is to cry
Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A gap where a woman was discovered.
explanation.walkthrough: The number points to 17 down, whose sense of sobbing gives CRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A cranny is a small narrow opening or chink.

clue.text: Sue illuminated one's entrance

parts.note: lit means illuminated
I is the Roman numeral one
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Sue lit up the entrance of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like a woman's name but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To litigate is to take legal action, to sue someone.
